package_info.package_versions: All versions used in Barracuda ESG prior to the patch for CVE-2023-7102
package_info.why_malicious: Spreadsheet::ParseExcel was exploited as part of a supply chain attack due to a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2023-7102) that allowed attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution by submitting specially crafted Excel files. While the package itself is not inherently malicious, its vulnerability enabled attackers to execute malicious payloads on Barracuda ESG appliances during email attachment scanning.

execution_context.file_location: Spreadsheet/ParseExcel.pm (invoked by Amavis virus scanner within Barracuda ESG)
required_permissions: filesystem access (to read/write temporary files and execute commands)
network access (if payload initiates outbound connections)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker-supplied, specially crafted Excel file exploits a vulnerability in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel, resulting in arbitrary code execution when the file is parsed.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During email attachment scanning, the Amavis scanner invokes Spreadsheet::ParseExcel to parse an attacker-crafted Excel file, which exploits a vulnerability in the library, allowing attacker-controlled code to execute on the ESG appliance, potentially leading to further compromise or malware deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path allows untrusted, attacker-supplied Excel files to trigger arbitrary code execution within a privileged context, which is a classic exploitation vector for remote code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects the library to safely parse Excel files for data extraction or malware scanning without executing any embedded code. Instead, the vulnerability allows attacker-controlled input to execute arbitrary commands on the system.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use involves parsing Excel files for extracting data or scanning for malware, never for executing code based on file content.
key_indicators: Parsing of malformed or non-standard Excel files leads to process spawning or command execution
Arbitrary code execution is triggered by attacker-supplied input during file parsing
Exploit is activated in the context of email attachment scanning on Barracuda ESG appliances
Unexpected creation of temporary files or scripts during Excel file processing

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted Excel file as an email attachment to a target organization using Barracuda ESG.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious file is received and queued for scanning by Amavis, which invokes Spreadsheet::ParseExcel.

attack_chain.action: Amavis virus scanner processes the attachment, calling Spreadsheet::ParseExcel to parse the Excel file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Vulnerability in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel is triggered by the crafted file.

attack_chain.action: Exploit in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel allows arbitrary code execution on the Barracuda ESG appliance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution, enabling further compromise or malware deployment on the ESG appliance.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process spawning or command execution by Amavis or Perl interpreter during Excel file parsing
Unusual network connections initiated by the ESG appliance immediately after email attachment scanning
Crashes, segmentation faults, or instability in Amavis or Spreadsheet::ParseExcel when handling Excel attachments
Creation of unexpected temporary files or scripts in directories used by Amavis or the Perl interpreter
file_indicators: Excel files with malformed or non-standard BIFF records targeting Spreadsheet::ParseExcel's parsing logic
Presence of temporary files or scripts with suspicious names or content created during email scanning
Excel attachments with embedded payloads designed to exploit CVE-2023-7102
network_indicators: Outbound connections from ESG appliances to external IPs or domains not associated with normal operation, following email scanning
Command-and-control (C2) traffic patterns originating from ESG appliances after processing Excel attachments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Barracuda ESG appliances for abnormal process activity or command execution by Amavis or Perl during or immediately after email attachment scanning, especially when handling Excel files. Inspect system and application logs for errors, crashes, or segmentation faults in Amavis or Spreadsheet::ParseExcel. Analyze incoming Excel attachments for exploit attempts targeting CVE-2023-7102, focusing on malformed BIFF records or non-standard structures. Correlate these events with unexpected outbound network connections or C2 traffic from ESG devices to identify potential compromise.
